findings.description: `validRetry` in `web/check.js` bounds the incoming `pushes` array with the inline literal `50` (`p.pushes.length <= 50`), and it repeats the inline `50` for `devs` in the same expression. The cap admits or rejects incoming peer messages, so it is a resource-admission limit, and the repo convention is to name such limits in `LIMITS` (used elsewhere in `check.js`, `net.js` and `index.html`). A later reader who wants to tune the batch bound has to find and change both literals, and nothing ties them to the sender's `MAX_BATCH` of 8 in `web/net.js`.
findings.title: Retry validator hard-codes its size cap

citations.citation: const EDGES = { L: 1, R: 1, T: 1, B: 1 }, MAX_BATCH = 8, PER_DEV = 2, DEADLINE = 2500;

findings.description: `s.push` keys its waits only by `s.now()` and replaces the existing wait when two pushes have the same timestamp. If the first push joins while the second gets no result, the first join clears the second push’s only fallback timer, so the second push never shows “No match.”
findings.title: A rapid second push gets no answer

evidence.explanation: The new push path replaces a timer already stored under the same timestamp, and result processing clears waits by timestamp alone. The new test confirms two same-millisecond pushes share one wait and that a single result stops it; matching can leave one of a device’s pushes unmatched.

findings.description: The new join checks in `tests/two-browser.mjs` and `tests/net.test.mjs` start every join through direct `net.push` calls, so no test sends a tap from a strip or a tap position. Non-facing taps, endpoint positions and default keyboard positions are never exercised. Strip-based stacking and overlap are deferred by the author's stated scope, so this is a known gap rather than a defect in the shipped path, but a later change could join ineligible taps without any failing check.
findings.title: Join tests skip non-facing and edge taps

findings.description: `evidence/day-08/repro/harness.mjs` imports the literal placeholder `'<checkout>/web/net.js'`, and `evidence/day-08/blind/harness.mjs` imports `'../code/web/net.js'`, a folder that is not in the repo. Every `r1`–`r3`, `q2` and `q3` script depends on one of these harnesses, so nobody can rerun the reproductions behind the verdicts in `02-findings-and-verdicts.md` from the committed tree. Separately, `r2.mjs` logs times using `A.heard.start`, which is never set, so it prints `NaN` even once the import is fixed.
findings.title: The committed reproduction scripts cannot be run
